summary.text: Randy Villegas is the Democratic nominee for California's 22nd District. A Bakersfield native and the son of immigrants, he is a political science professor at College of the Sequoias and a Visalia Unified School District trustee, and previously worked as a journalist and community organizer. He is running on Medicare for All, workers' rights and a pledge not to take corporate PAC money, according to his Ballotpedia survey.

paragraphs.text: Born and raised in Kern County, California, in a working-class family; the son of immigrants, he says he grew up in Bakersfield and attended Golden Valley High School. He co-owns his family's auto shop, according to a KGET interview.

Earned an associate degree in political science from Bakersfield College (2015), a bachelor's degree in political science from CSU Bakersfield (2017), and a master's degree and a Ph.D. in Politics (with an emphasis in Latin American and Latino Studies) from UC Santa Cruz (Ph.D. 2022).

Before graduate school he worked as a journalist and community organizer in Bakersfield, and has written articles and opinion pieces for outlets including the Los Angeles Times and the Bakersfield Californian.

Teaches political science at College of the Sequoias in Visalia, where he was an associate professor as of 2021; he received the American Political Science Association's 2025 Community College Faculty Award.

Provisionally appointed to the Visalia Unified School District Board (Trustee Area 6) in December 2021 and elected to the seat in November 2022. He says he has won pay increases for teachers and staff.

Has served on the boards of the nonprofits Power California and Alisal Community Arts Network and as a volunteer drumline instructor at a local high school, according to the district's 2021 announcement.

Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary. Endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, Dolores Huerta, the California Nurses Association, the California Teachers Association, the United Auto Workers, Latino Victory Fund, and the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.
